title: A long-term gridded dataset of aboveground net primary productivity for global natural grasslands
abstract: A long-term dataset of aboveground net primary productivity (ANPP) for global natural grasslands is essential for carbon dynamics modeling and sustainable land management. However, existing datasets are limited: they often fail to separate above- and below-ground productivity or reflect only post-disturbance conditions. To address these gaps, we developed a gridded annual ANPP dataset using machine learning, spanning historical (1958-2023) and future (2015-2100) periods. Historical ANPP data were derived from TerraClimate at 1/24° spatial resolution, while future projections came from CMIP6 models under SSP245 and SSP585 scenarios at 1/2° resolution. Our model performed robustly (R<sup>2</sup> = 0.675 ± 0.009), showing temporal and spatial reliability through cross-validation with published products. Notably, systematic ANPP underestimation occurs in high-productivity regions (>700 g m<sup>-2</sup>) due to sparse field observations, so values in these areas should be interpreted with caution. Our dataset provides a spatially explicit baseline of climate-driven productivity, supporting precise evaluation of human impacts on grasslands and informing adaptive management under climate change.
problem: Existing datasets for grassland aboveground net primary productivity are limited as they often fail to separate above- and below-ground components, reflect post-disturbance conditions, or lack the annual, long-term temporal resolution necessary for accurate carbon dynamics modeling and sustainable land management.
method: This study developed a long-term gridded dataset of aboveground net primary productivity for global natural grasslands using a machine learning model that integrates multi-year mean productivity data with annual climate anomalies to capture interannual variability.
task: The task is to develop a long-term gridded dataset of aboveground net primary productivity for global natural grasslands, spanning historical and future periods, by using a machine learning model that integrates field measurements with climate data.
innovation: This paper presents a machine learning-derived, long-term gridded dataset of aboveground net primary productivity for global natural grasslands, spanning historical (1958–2023) and future (2015–2100) periods to provide a baseline of climate-driven productivity under undisturbed conditions.

Ultimately, we established a gridded annual ANPP dataset for global natural grasslands 16, consisting of two subsets: one based on the TerraClimate database, spanning 1958–2023 at 1/24° resolution; the other derived from CMIP6 projections under SSP245 and SSP585 climate scenarios, from 2015 to 2100 at 1/2° resolution.
